messages.subject: Calibration Data for Error Model
parts:
Hi all, 
in accounting for location error, can we use horizontal accuracy (metres) from tracking data instead of HDOP from calibrated trackers? 
Many thanks, 
Aaron

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Calibration Data for Error Model
parts:
Hi Aaron,

Even better is to test both the horizontal accuracy and HDOP on calibration data - especially because the proportionality constant for horizontal accuracy may not be 1.0

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Calibration Data for Error Model
parts:
Hi Christen, 
I conducted a small calibration data collection for my gps collars. I stationed 3 collars in an open field location and 3 collars in an hedgerow adjacent location. Each collar collected 72 fixes in total over two days. 
I looked at model selection values for individual collars in both habitats and thankfully, the individual error models had very similar results to joint models. 
I then compared joint habitat model selection values with individual habitat model selection values and this was the result I got: 


Vertical values are very similar, however there is a moderate difference between the horizontal AICc values. The difference in reduced z-squared value is relatively small. In your vignette for error data, you caution against selecting based on AICc values, if differences are somewhat similar. Do you think these differences necessitate a larger collection of gps in both habitats ?

Thanks for your help, 
Aaron
